title: When fixing the audit creates a new audit subject
summary: Endaoment fixed major governance issues through a broad refactor; OpenZeppelin then warned that the resulting codebase may itself merit another restricted audit.

case_study.situation: OpenZeppelin's engagement found major governance restrictions that Endaoment needed to change before production. The fixes landed across two pull requests and materially reorganized the contracts.
case_study.turning_point: The audit update accepted the reported fixes but warned that implementing them had produced a substantially different codebase from the one originally reviewed.
case_study.lesson: A remediation review can close named findings without extending the original audit boundary over everything the remediation changed. Successful fixes may create a new review subject.

claim: Resolution of the reported major findings is sufficient evidence that the materially refactored system is ready for production.
evidence_boundary: The audit update records finding-level fixes, not comprehensive coverage of the substantially changed codebase, its configured roles, or a deployed instance.

decision.question: Should the original audit plus fix review be treated as coverage of the refactored production candidate?
decision.expected: Request a targeted re-audit and deployment/configuration evidence; the auditor explicitly says the fixes produced a substantially different codebase.

missing_edges: A defined restricted re-audit scope for the materially changed contracts.
Evidence that production role configuration and deployed bytecode match the reviewed system.

recommendations.action: Commission a restricted audit of the materially refactored contracts.
recommendations.because: The auditor explicitly warned that the fixes produced a substantially different codebase.

recommendations.action: Record production roles and deployed bytecode against the reviewed candidate.
recommendations.because: Finding-level closure does not establish the configuration or identity of the production system.
